notes:
Order: each two-column block is given left column top to bottom, then right column (block 1: 1–29 then 30–65; block 2: Scotland W 81–114 and Isle of Man 115–118, then England W 119–162; Ireland 1–19 then 20–40), then Outlying Stations. Rows from different columns share line numbers. Fragments are trimmed of the layout whitespace around them; nothing else is changed.

The list itself: it names no keepers, gives no light characters, and has no return marks (no * or † flags for returns). The only marks are the braces "{" on 11/12 Hoy Sound (Low)/(High), which pair the two Hoy Sound lights. Numbers 66–80 are not used (the gap between England E and Scotland W).

Rows 1–3_b_ (Iceland, Do., Faroe, Fair Isle) have no heading. "England--East Coast" is printed on line 141 but it heads the right-hand column, so I gave these rows coast null. Row 2 "Do." is a ditto, i.e. a second Iceland station; its name is kept as "Do.".

Ireland uses its own numbers starting again at 1. 9 and 35 are missing, and 5* and 8* are inserted numbers. I put the asterisk in number ("5*", "8*") and gave marks null, because it reads as a sub-number like 3_b_ and not as a returns mark. "5*.Coningbeg" and "8*.Arklow" have no space after the dot in the print.

Dates and notes in brackets went into other: Fidra "(1885)", Langness "(1880)", Ailsa Craig "(building, 1885)" (wrapped onto line 213). Skerryvore wraps onto line 195 ("Signal Tower, Tiree."). I read it as the single entry "Skerryvore and Hynish Signal Tower" with place "Tiree"; you could split it into two stations. English and Welsh Grounds L.V. wraps onto line 207. Where a locality follows a comma I put it in place: Fladda/Easdale, Pladda/Arran, Old Head/Kinsale ("Old Head of Kinsale" is arguably all one name), Blackrock/Mayo, Stevns Fyr/Zealand, Malmo/Sweden, Casquets/Alderney, Hanois/Guernsey. The compass letters in "Eagle Island, E.", "Slyne Head, N." and similar are kept as part of the name.

Hasbro' appears twice, as 42 L.V. and 46 L.H.

Spellings kept as printed (modern form in brackets): Whalsey (Whalsay), N. Ronaldshay, Girdleness, Montroseness, Llyn Wells (Lynn Well), Hasbro' (Happisburgh), Languard Point (Landguard), Rhu Stoir, Island Ghlais (Eilean Glas), Dhuheartach (Dubh Artach), Rhuvaal, Skervuile, Lochindaul, Devaar (Davaar), Chickens Rock, Air (Point of Ayr), Great Castlehead, Caldy, Wolf-Rock, Howth Baily, Innishtrahull, Arran Island (Aran), Malmo (no umlaut).
